reason: This paper directly studies how LLM inference serving systems should be evaluated: it identifies baseline fairness, workload selection, latency/SLO and metric-design pitfalls, then demonstrates the issues through speculative decoding. It contributes an evaluation checklist and empirical analysis rather than an inference-serving mechanism or an efficiency improvement itself. Retained as borderline because its object is LLM inference-system performance and reproducibility, while its contribution is methodological evaluation rather than system optimization.
title: On Evaluating Performance of LLM Inference Systems
